assumptions: Mott's algorithm as the instrument recorded it, or a quality window at the threshold given.
bio.jane/contract.question: Where should this read's low-quality ends be cut, by the method named?

description: Trim a Sanger read's low-quality ends, by either of the two methods that answer different questions: the instrument's own Mott record as written into the file, or a sliding mean-Phred window computed here. Returns the kept interval as 1-based inclusive bounds, and the mean quality of what it KEPT beside the mean of what it DISCARDED — the pair that says whether the trim was worth making, because a trim whose discarded ends score no worse than the bases it left has shortened the read for nothing.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

document.description: which trace file to read: its name (`read_F.ab1`) or its project file id. A file id is project-specific, so a template ships this unset.

method.description: auto = the file's own Mott record when it has one and the sliding window when it does not; mott = the instrument's record, which SCF and ZTR never carry; window = always compute it here.

min_q.description: the mean Phred the window has to hold for a bound to stop walking inward.

win_size.description: bases in the sliding window, when the window method runs.

name: trim_trace

firstBaseKept.description: 1-based inclusive, matching every trim readout in the editor

keptBases.description: how many bases survived. Wire it into a gate: a read trimmed to nothing is not a read

meanQualityDiscarded.description: mean Phred over what was cut. Read it AGAINST the kept figure: if it is not lower, the trim removed nothing bad

meanQualityKept.description: mean Phred over the kept interval

methodUsed.description: which one actually ran. `auto` and `mott` both answer `window` when the file carries no Mott record, and a pipeline that assumed otherwise trimmed on a threshold nobody chose

reading.description: the same sentence the editor shows for this run, generated from it

sequence.description: the trimmed read, ready to align or verify
